gap: No result ChatGPT got states, for any one-listing kit near 10 kWh, the price per Wh together with the full-sun hours its own panels need to refill it: Sun Gold Power SGR-8K10E is about $0.48/Wh and 2.8 h, BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2× B300K + 2× 500 W is $0.63/Wh and 8.3 h, the same BLUETTI with 2× 200 W is $0.53/Wh and 20.7 h, and Jackery's 10 kWh / 1,000 W kit is about $0.84/Wh and 10.1 h.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages I could open plus three top results. StormWatts '5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input' (cited) gives $/kWh for stations only and sun-hours with panels bought separately; its only 10 kWh figure is Jackery at $6,199 with no panels and no per-Wh. Solar Waypoint (cited) has no prices and no kits. EnergySage (cited) has no kit near 10 kWh and no refill hours. StormWatts 'Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts' computes $/kWh and refill for 24 kits, but its largest is 3,763 Wh and it explicitly leaves out the $8,499 Jackery 10 kWh set. Powersized 'Kits by Battery Size' says no kit of 4,500 Wh and up met its rules on Nov 18. ChatGPT's own answer has a generic panel-watts-to-days table (1,000 W = about 2.8 days), so the method is already on the shopper's screen; what is missing is the per-kit numbers at this size. Not a 3 because the kit that wins the arithmetic is a wired component kit whose dispatch date I could not read, and both of our in-range kits are pre-orders. solargenadvisor.com and theoutageplan.com kit pages failed to load (certificate error), so they are not compared.
decides: Size line 8,000-12,000 Wh (10 kWh ±20%). Only two kits we link fall inside it, both BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2× B300K (8,294.4 Wh), and both are pre-orders with store dispatch late January 2027, so neither can be the ships-now pick. On the arithmetic the Sun Gold Power SGR-8K10E (in our catalog, awin:sungoldpower, not in the 'Kits we link' table) wins: lowest price per Wh and the only kit whose own panels refill the battery inside one day. It is a wired inverter + rack-battery + rigid-panel kit, not a plug-in power station, and its dispatch date must be read before it is named the pick. Among plug-in kits, the BLUETTI with 2× 500 W is the one to name for a shopper who can wait: the extra $855 at the link price buys 600 W more panel and cuts refill from 20.7 h to 8.3 h. The 2× 200 W version is cheaper per Wh but takes about 5.8 sunny days to refill on ChatGPT's own assumptions. Jackery's 10 kWh kit costs about a third more per Wh than the BLUETTI 2× 500 W kit and is also a pre-order (station Dec 2, panels Dec 5). Just outside the line: Apex 300 + B500K + 500 W (7,884.8 Wh, 21% under), Apex 200 + B500K + 2× 500 W (7,680 Wh, 23% under), EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X 12 kWh (12,288 Wh, 23% over).
